"Agreement" (0–1) compares the features of a pair with its competing candidates and the option "no match". It is a ranking set by judgement, not a probability that the link is correct.

“Correct” confirms the link: an automatic link or proposal becomes confirmed. “Wrong” rejects the pair; with another visit, that visit is linked instead. Changing the verdict later undoes no link; links are changed in the review.
Linking records “partner missed” and confirms the link. Changing the verdict later undoes no link; links are changed in the review.
“Unclear”: you looked and cannot decide; it counts as judged and is left out of the share. “Skip”: decide later; nothing is recorded, the case stays open and the next open case follows.

ORBIS: export the ED list with the MTS triage (one row per ED visit) as a CSV file with semicolons and all columns, for a closed period, for example one month. The tool keeps only the fields it needs and drops names, dates of birth, staff and free text. It recognises the export by these columns:
Other systems need a profile of their own. If your system is not listed, contact the project team with the column names of your export (no data).

Create the key file once per hospital in the tool ("No key file yet? Create one"), save it in a team folder that everyone who prepares data can reach, and use the same file for every run. Never send it to anyone and never upload it.

Assigns your hospital's department codes, stations and discharge texts. You need it when the tool's report lists "unmapped values" for the department, the care level or the disposition. Fill it in the tool; it stays on your computer.

Open the downloaded file in a current browser, load the key file, the local map if any and the export, and start the preparation. Check the report, the content check and the preview of the first rows, then save the file.

Upload the saved file as "Encounter data (beta)" for your hospital and confirm that it was made with the tool. After the import, the visits are matched with the IVENA allocations; proposed links are reviewed in the match review.

The key file lets the tool turn the case number into a pseudonym. The same case gives the same pseudonym with the same key, so a visit uploaded twice is recognised, and the server never learns the case number.
The server only knows a check value of the key. The first upload registers it; files with another key are rejected.

Changing the key starts a new key generation: everyone needs the new key file, and visits of the old generation can no longer be recognised in new uploads. The person changing the key chooses whether the data uploaded so far is deleted (then every period can be uploaded again) or kept (then only upload new periods).
Lost the key file, or someone unauthorised may have seen it? Then the key has to be changed. Nobody can restore a lost key, not even the project team.

As an administrator you can change the key of every hospital from its edit pages.
Only the owner of the hospital or an administrator can change the key. Contact them if the key file is lost.
